title: Composite signal governor for cost-aware automated rollback with hysteresis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a composite-guard mechanism that triggers automated rollback or staged traffic reduction for canary/A-B/shadow rollouts by combining latency, error-rate, token-cost, and throughput signals into a single governance score. The governor introduces metric-specific hysteresis windows, minimum evaluation durations, and a tunable cooldown to reduce false positives. We will also surface a human-friendly severity band in the Console and expose per-route override controls.

Motivation: existing single-threshold triggers are noisy (especially for token-cost spikes caused by prompt shifts) and either cause unnecessary rollbacks or silently allow regressions. The new approach should: 1) detect meaningful degradations across multiple axes, 2) be robust to transient noise and traffic bursts, 3) allow SRE/PM to tune sensitivity per-customer and per-route, and 4) preserve low-latency for high-priority routes by favoring staged traffic-mitigation over full immediate reversion when safe.

Design summary: compute normalized z-scores for each SLO signal (latency P95, request error-rate, token-cost-per-request, throughput deviation), apply a configurable weight vector, and produce a composite severity score. Apply two-stage decisioning: detection (statistical evidence via Bayesian changepoint or sequential probability ratio test over rolling window) and action (graded response: alert-only -> restrict-rate -> shift-to-stable-model-variant -> rollback). Hysteresis parameters: separate warmup window, minimum sustained deviation duration, and cooldown that scales with per-route risk. Integrations: Console notifications, Slack/SRE runbook link, metrics exported to Grafana, and audit trail to the Private deployment's audit logs.

Constraints and trade-offs: Bayesian detectors reduce delay on real regressions but are computationally heavier; we will run them on aggregated rollup streams (per-canary cohort) not per-request. Token-cost signal requires correlating prompt-type cohorts; initial implementation will use route-level aggregates with a follow-up cohorting pass. Tunability vs safety: default presets will be conservative; aggressive tuning will be opt-in for internal platforms customers.

Success criteria: reduce false-positive automated rollbacks by >=50% vs baseline while maintaining time-to-detect for real regressions within the same SLO band. Provide observability to explain why a rollback was triggered (top contributing signals).
acceptance_criteria: Composite severity score implemented and stored as time-series for canaries
Detection and action policy engine integrated into rollout controller
Console shows contributing signal breakdown and severity band for each triggered action
Feature flag to toggle automatic actions per-organization
End-to-end test harness with synthetic regressions for latency, error-rate, and token-cost
Documentation and runbook published with example tuning presets
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Initial design doc posted. Requesting feedback from runtime and console teams on the 'graded response' lifecycle. Linked prototype notebook that computes z-scores on historical rollouts.

2026-02-12 - Miguel Ortega: Spike detection prototype (bayes-detector) merged to feature/eng-112233. Benchmarked on staging: detects sustained P95 latency regressions within ~45s on 30s window; false-positive rate down ~40% vs simple threshold in our test corpus.

2026-02-13 - Sasha Ivanov (Console): Adding a compact UI artifact to present 'top 3 contributing signals' — will use existing per-route metric breakdown components. Need a small API contract change (events:severity, contributors).

2026-02-14 - Security (review request): flagged token-cost signal derivation as potentially exposing prompt contents. Recommendation: only use aggregated token counts per-route and make token-cohort IDs opaque. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-02-15 - Miguel Ortega: Ran ablation where token-cost weight set to 0.5 vs 0.1; higher weight catches cost regressions earlier but increased noisy action on beta routes where prompt mix varies. Decided default weight for token-cost = 0.15 and provide an 'aggressive-cost' profile for internal teams.

2026-02-16 - SRE (ops): Proposed default cooldown of 10 minutes for production canaries, 2 minutes for internal dev lanes. Also requested a manual 'pause auto-actions' toggle tied to incident status in Console.

2026-02-16 - Miguel Ortega: Created PR #2345 for policy engine and PR #2358 for metrics export. Running integration tests against dedicated staging and will run chaos test to validate graceful staged rollbacks. Next: finalize UI contract and complete security remediation steps for token-count aggregation.
